title: Ben in cowboy gear, with his dog, riding at Rock Creek Park
summary: Ben buys western boots, a Stetson and a stray dog and books six o'clock rides at a stable in Rock Creek Park, and Leeman cooks daily at friends' houses.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: They just adored Ben Webster. And we went over and rehearsed and it was a day ahead of opening, and we rehearsed for awhile, and Ben called the rehearsal off and took me with him, he couldn't stand it any more, because we had to go to a sporting goods store and look all over for someplace that carried western gear. And we found him a beautiful pair of black boots. He never had them off in the 8 to 10 weeks that we were down there. He made quite a sight going to work, and he got a Stetson, a beautiful Stetson western hat, and it was western hat, and at that time Ben was into carrying hand-tooled silver canes, and walking sticks. He loved walking sticks, and he had a dog at the pound around there -- Ben couldn't stand to see anything destroyed, so he went over and got himself an old dog,

a scraggly old thing, and Ben had him all washed and he would walk down the street going to work with his horn under one arm, his walking stick in the other hand, and his Stetson, as I said, and his cowboy boots, and a beautiful $300 hand-tailored suit, and with the dog in tow. And it was quite an entourage. Frank Sinatra would be very proud of that one. On our way to work ...

And Ben set this whole thing up to be the play period in his life. Music wasn't incidental because we were all serious about our playing nights, but he had us all set up, we'd go to bed at one, two, two thirty in the morning, or rather we'd stay out late drinking and got through at that time, and he had a six o'clock appointment for the next 8 to 10 weeks that we were there, with a stables, and it happened to be a stable in Rock Creek Park.

And we'd get up at six or seven o'clock in the morning with very little sleep, and still stoned, and go riding. And we did this morning after morning and day in and day out. And then he would set up with some of the lovely people he knew there, and he liked my cooking, and I had to cook every day. Ben would buy the groceries, and we'd go to somebody else's house every day. And I'd cook the meal.
We're continuing with the Ben Webster
